name: Mentoring and Digital Wellbeing
title: Mentoring and Digital Wellbeing
answer: Mentoring programs pair students with supportive adults, and AI in spreadsheets can suggest possible matches based on interests and needs, though the coordinator makes the final decision. Students also need lessons on digital wellbeing, which teachers can lead without special products, and social and emotional learning lessons can be drafted with AI help and then adapted and checked by the teacher.

sections.body: This idea combines mentoring, digital wellbeing education, and social and emotional learning support. It solves the problem of connecting students to adults who can help them and of teaching students to manage their own technology use and emotions. AI can suggest mentor matches and draft lesson plans, which saves time and surfaces options. The program coordinator still decides the final mentor matches using personal knowledge of students and mentors. A good match depends on human understanding, and the lessons that reach students are delivered by people who know them.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In a school, a mentoring coordinator can use spreadsheet features to generate suggested pairings of students and mentors based on interests and needs, then review those suggestions and make the final matches personally. Teachers can lead lessons on screen time, social media, and healthy habits without any special product, helping students make choices that support their wellbeing. For social and emotional learning, a teacher might use MagicSchool to draft lessons on managing emotions, building friendships, or handling stress. The teacher then adapts the lessons to their students and checks that the content is sound. The lessons themselves are delivered by people who know the students.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text reports one study finding: a survey of 3,378 middle school students in China found that more than three hours a day of entertainment internet use was linked to more anxiety and depression, while moderate gaming was not harmful (Li et al., 2023). The text gives no evidence label for the mentoring or social and emotional learning parts of the idea, so those rest on practice rather than research.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The program coordinator makes the final mentor matches, using what they know about students and mentors, because a good match is built on human understanding. Teachers adapt AI-drafted social and emotional learning lessons to their students and check that the content is sound. The lessons themselves are delivered by people who know the students. Digital wellbeing lessons can be led by teachers without any special product. The decisions about who mentors whom and what students are taught stay with the people in the school.
